## Summary

Tetraphenylcyclopentadienone and diphenylacetylene form hexaphenylbenzene with loss of carbon monoxide. This is sample data; the quantities are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tetraphenylcyclopentadienone | 479-33-4 | 384.48 | 0.769 g | 2 | 1.0 |
| Diphenylacetylene | 501-65-5 | 178.23 | 0.392 g | 2.2 | 1.1 |
| Benzophenone | 119-61-9 | 182.22 | 5 g | – | – |
| Toluene | 108-88-3 | 92.14 | for dilution and washing, as needed | – | – |
| Diphenyl ether | 101-84-8 | 170.21 | for recrystallisation, as needed | – | – |

## Procedure

1. Charge a flask with tetraphenylcyclopentadienone, diphenylacetylene and benzophenone.
2. Fit a condenser to a vented apparatus in a functioning fume hood.
3. Heat the stirred mixture to reflux at about 300 °C.
4. Maintain reflux for 90 minutes while carbon monoxide is released.
5. Switch off the heat and allow the apparatus to cool well below the boiling point of toluene.
6. Add toluene cautiously to dilute the cooled mixture.

## Workup and Purification

Collect the solid by suction filtration and wash with toluene. Recrystallise from hot diphenyl ether, cool, filter and dry. Expected yield: 0.75 g (1.40 mmol, 70 %).

## Characterization

White crystals; aromatic ¹H NMR signals are expected around δ 6.5–7.2.

## Notes

1. Never seal the apparatus: carbon monoxide is evolved.
2. Keep the hot apparatus in the hood until cool.
3. Use only a small amount of hot diphenyl ether for recrystallisation.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Carbon monoxide: toxic gas evolved during the reaction; vent into the fume hood. Tetraphenylcyclopentadienone: dust may irritate skin and eyes; Diphenylacetylene: may irritate skin and eyes; Benzophenone: harmful if swallowed; suspected of causing cancer; may cause organ damage through prolonged or repeated exposure; hazardous to aquatic life; Toluene: highly flammable; harmful by inhalation and suspected of damaging the unborn child; Diphenyl ether: harmful if swallowed; hazardous to aquatic life; Hexaphenylbenzene: may irritate skin and eyes. Work in a fume hood; wear gloves and eye protection. Collect toluene, benzophenone and diphenyl ether filtrates as organic waste.

## References

1. Fieser, L. F. Hexaphenylbenzene. Org. Synth. 1966, 46, 44.
